column2: The defenders are dead or fled, and the people of [From.GetName] cower in their cellars and barns. My warriors drag them out by the hair and rope them neck to neck: men for the oar and the mine, women and children for the markets. A fine haul. They will fetch a good price, or work my own lands until they drop.

The raid on [From.GetName] has gone well. Chains are hammered shut on the necks of the surviving folk, and they are driven to the black arks to be sold in the markets of Karond Kar, or broken in my own fields and mines. Those who die on the way are thrown to the sea, or kept for the altars of Khaine.
Chain them all. Every one of them has a price.
Their blood belongs to the gods. Kill them on the altar.
Leave them. Their misery is enough.
My pens hold captives enough to sell. The slave dealers have come to haggle. How many will I sell?
Sell a whole column of them.

Slaves do not need wages, only whips and bread. A column of my captives can dig the mines and fields of [From.GetName] for years before they are worked to death, though the locals fear them, and fear what happens when they rise.
Keep them in the pens for now.
